name: Ossic Fracture Charge OFC-7 'Jawbreaker'
description: The OFC-7 is a proximity-triggered blast device engineered around a narrow-band resonant frequency array embedded in its casing. Rather than relying on fragmentation or raw overpressure, the charge detonates with a precisely shaped acoustic shockwave tuned to the resonant frequency of human bone — specifically the skull, jaw, and orbital structures. The initial concussive blast is comparatively mild; it is the secondary resonant pulse lasting 0.08 seconds that causes the characteristic bilateral temporal fractures and sinus cavity collapse that give the weapon its street name.
specifications:
weight: 0.6 kg
diameter: 9 cm
trigger modes: Proximity (adjustable 0.5–3 m), Remote detonation, Timer (1–30 seconds)
effective kill radius: 2.5 m
effective injury radius: 6 m
resonant frequency: Classified — estimated 210–240 Hz burst sweep
casing: Low-radar-return polymer composite
tactical_use: Used almost exclusively in assassination and targeted elimination operations where collateral structural damage must be minimized — the OFC-7 kills people in a room while leaving the room largely intact. Security contractors plant them under chairs, inside door frames, or beneath flooring panels. The injury radius produces immediate incapacitation through vertigo, tinnitus, and jaw dislocation, which makes it useful for capture operations when set to low-yield mode.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's corporate espionage circles, receiving an OFC-7 in a parcel — unarmed, as a message — is a well-understood death threat. The weapon's clinical precision has made it a status symbol among high-end fixers who want to signal they can afford surgical solutions. ZHENG-DAO officially denies manufacturing it, though their component signatures are unmistakable to anyone with a spectral analyzer.
known_users: High-end fixers operating in executive districts
story_hooks: A city councilor survives an OFC-7 detonation that should have been fatal — someone swapped the resonance array for a dummy, and the councilor wants to know who saved them and why.
A fixer's safe house is swept and three OFC-7 charges are found inside the walls, already armed. The fixer has no idea who planted them or how long they've been there.
ZHENG-DAO's denial of the OFC-7's existence becomes legally complicated when a forensics team recovers an intact unit with a factory serial number still etched on the internal housing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, almost medical-looking sphere with a subtly asymmetrical geometry—smoothly contoured but with barely-visible geometric faceting along its equator suggesting internal resonance chambers. The silhouette is deceptively benign, resembling a high-end medical implant or industrial sensor rather than a weapon.
physical_description.dimensions: 9 cm diameter (spherical), approximately 8 cm tall when accounting for the trigger interface nub on the crown
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and balanced despite its small size—0.6 kg feels substantial in the palm, the weight distributed evenly giving it an unsettling, almost organic heft
physical_description.primary_material: Low-radar-return polymer composite with reinforced nano-lattice structure, slightly translucent under certain angles revealing faint internal geometric patterning
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with an imperceptible iridescence—shifts between flat black and deep indigo depending on light angle, suggesting advanced light-absorbing coating rather than traditional paint
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Charcoal matte black with dark slate undertones. Accents: Faint bioluminescent green trace lines following internal resonance chamber topology (visible only when armed)
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured micro-grip polymer with dissipative properties—slightly cool to touch, faintly granular, designed to prevent accidental triggering while maintaining secure purchase
distinctive_features: Crown-mounted trigger interface: recessed nub with microscopic haptic feedback dimples
Equatorial band of minute perforations (0.3mm) revealing the resonance chamber lattice beneath
Three flush-mounted indicator nodes at cardinal points: armed status (green), frequency lock (amber), battery/charge state (red)
Serial plate embedded flush into the casing: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC cipher-stamped in micro-characters
Faint ghosted grid pattern across the surface from internal piezoelectric array alignment
Microscopic thermal relief vents clustered near the base
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC corporate ideogram laser-etched into a recessed pocket on the lower hemisphere; serial/batch designation stamped in nano-characters on a flush-mounted tungsten plate; no visible model designation—security through obscurity
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show minimal wear due to careful handling requirements—light scuff marks from secure storage, occasional discoloration from residue sampling, and occasional micro-abrasions on the trigger nub from repeated arming cycles. Black market units may show evidence of field modification or jury-rigged remote triggers soldered to the interface
